spots.name: Warrior on Horseback
spots.summary: Warrior on Horseback, also translated as Warrior on a Horse, is a monument in Macedonia Square in Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia. The monument consists of a 12-metre bronze statue, on top of a 10-metre pedestal including a fountain. The monument was installed as part of the Skopje 2014 infrastructure project.

spots.name: Stone Bridge
spots.summary: The Stone Bridge is a bridge across the Vardar River in Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia, built by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror.

spots.name: Macedonia Square
spots.summary: Macedonia Square is the main square of Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia. The square is the biggest in North Macedonia with a total extent of 18,500 m2. It is located in the central part of the city, and it crosses the Vardar River.

spots.name: Vodno
spots.summary: Vodno is a mountain in North Macedonia. It is located in the northern part of the country, to the southwest of the capital city Skopje. The highest point of the mountain is on Krstovar peak, at 1066 meters and the submontane is at 337 meters.

spots.name: Millennium Cross
spots.summary: The Millennium Cross is a 66-metre (217 ft) tall cross situated on the top of Vodno Mountain in North Macedonia above the capital city of Skopje. Built in 2002, it is one of the tallest crosses worldwide.

spots.name: Memorial House of Mother Teresa

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Mother Teresa Memorial House is a museum dedicated to the Catholic saint and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Mother Teresa. It is located in her hometown Skopje, in North Macedonia, where she lived from 1910 to 1928.

spots.name: Old Bazaar
spots.summary: The Old Bazaar also known as Turkish Bazaar is a bazaar located in Skopje, North Macedonia, situated on the eastern bank of the Vardar River, stretching from the Stone Bridge to the Bit-Pazar and from the Skopje Fortress to the Serava river.

spots.name: Church of St. Clement of Ohrid

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Clement of Ohrid, often called simply the Soborna Crkva, is a cathedral church of the Macedonian Orthodox Church, located in Skopje, North Macedonia. It is the largest cathedral of the Macedonian Orthodox Church.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St. Clement of Ohrid

spots.name: Skopje Fortress
spots.summary: The Skopje Fortress, commonly referred to as Kale, is a historic fortress located in the old town of Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia. It is located in Centar municipality and situated on the highest point in the city overlooking the Vardar River.

spots.name: Porta Macedonia

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Porta Macedonia is a memorial arch located on Pella Square in Skopje, North Macedonia. Construction started in 2011 and was completed in January 2012.

spots.name: Mustafa Pasha Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Mustafa Pasha Mosque is an Ottoman-era mosque located in the Old Bazaar of Skopje, North Macedonia.

spots.name: Church of St. Panteleimon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Panteleimon in Gorno Nerezi, North Macedonia, is a small 12th-century Byzantine church located in a monastery complex. Built in 1164, is dedicated to the patron saint of physicians, St. Panteleimon.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St. Panteleimon, Gorno Nerezi

spots.name: Skopje Aqueduct

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Skopje Aqueduct is an aqueduct and archaeological site located in the neighbourhood of Vizbegovo, 2 km (1.2 mi) northwest of central Skopje, North Macedonia.

spots.name: Church of the Ascension of Jesus, Skopje

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Church of the Ascension of Jesus is an Eastern Orthodox church in Skopje, North Macedonia. It is situated east of Kale Fortress.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of the Ascension of Jesus, Skopje

spots.name: Skopje Zoo
spots.summary: The Skopje Zoo is a 12-hectare (30-acre) zoo near City Park in Skopje, North Macedonia. It is home to 500 animals representing 85 species.

spots.name: Kuršumli An
spots.summary: Kursumli An is an Ottoman caravanserai located in the Old Town of Skopje. It is in the area of Museum of Macedonia. It has served as an inn and as a prison.

spots.name: Museum of the Macedonian Struggle

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museum of the Macedonian Struggle is a national museum of North Macedonia located in the capital city of Skopje. Construction of the museum began on 11 June 2008 and it was opened to the public on the 20th anniversary of the declaration of independence on 8 September 2011.

spots.name: Church of Sts. Constantine and Helena

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Sts. Constantine and Helena is a Macedonian Orthodox church located on "Street Macedonia" in Skopje, North Macedonia. The church is a part of the project "Skopje 2014".
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Sts. Constantine and Helena (Skopje)

spots.name: Museum of the Republic of North Macedonia

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museum of the Republic of North Macedonia, formerly and still unofficially known as the Museum of Macedonia, is a national institution in Macedonia and one of the oldest museums in the country. It is located in the Old Bazaar in Skopje, near the Skopje Fortress.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of the Republic of North Macedonia

spots.name: Holocaust Memorial Center for the Jews of Macedonia

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Holocaust Memorial Center for the Jews of Macedonia is a memorial to the Holocaust of the 7,148 Jews from North Macedonia and the history of the Jews in the Balkans, located in Skopje, the capital city of North Macedonia.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Holocaust Memorial Center for the Jews of Macedonia

spots.name: Art Bridge
spots.summary: The Art Bridge is a pedestrian bridge across the Vardar River in the centre of Skopje, the capital city of North Macedonia. The bridge features many statues of noted Macedonian artists and musicians. It was built as part of the larger Skopje 2014 project, with an estimated construction cost of €2.5 million.

spots.name: Kapan Han
spots.summary: Kapan Han is a han (caravanserai) in the Old Bazaar of Skopje, North Macedonia. It was built in the mid-15th century by Bosnian general Isa-Beg Isaković, ruler of Skopsko Krajište, in order to provide a regular source of income for his endowment (vakuf).

spots.name: Čifte Hammam

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Čifte Hammam is a hammam in the Old Bazaar of Skopje, North Macedonia. It was built in the mid-15th century by Bosnian general Isa-Beg Ishaković in order to provide a regular source of income for his endowment.

spots.name: Suli An
spots.summary: The Suli An is a han in the Old Bazaar of Skopje, North Macedonia. It was built in the mid-15th century by Isa-Beg Isaković. Today, the building houses the permanent exhibition History of the Old Bazaar of the Museum of the City of Skopje.

spots.name: Skanderbeg Square
spots.summary: Skanderbeg Square is a square in Skopje, North Macedonia.

spots.name: National Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Gallery is a national art museum of North Macedonia in the Old Bazaar, located in the capital city of Skopje. Its permanent collection is housed in the 15th century hammam known as the Daut Pasha Baths, but the museum also features a smaller exhibition at the nearby Čifte Hammam.

spots.name: Archaeological Museum of North Macedonia

spots.summary: The Archaeological Museum of the Republic of North Macedonia is a archaeological museum in Skopje, North Macedonia.

spots.name: Museum of Contemporary Art

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Contemporary Art Museum is a contemporary art museum located in Skopje, North Macedonia. It is the biggest and most modern museum in the country. The museum was founded in 1963 following the disastrous earthquake that hit the city.

spots.name: Museum of the City of Skopje
spots.summary: The Museum of the City of Skopje is a complex city museum focusing on Skopje, capital of North Macedonia, development from its origins to the modern era. The museum is home to permanent еxhibitions representing the history of Skopje, from the first recorded settlements around 3000 BC to present.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of the City of Skopje

spots.name: Toše Proeski Arena
spots.summary: National Arena Toše Proeski is a sports stadium in Skopje, North Macedonia. It is currently used mostly for football matches, but also for concerts or athletics.

spots.name: Pella Square
spots.summary: The Pella Square is one of the main squares of Skopje, the capital city of North Macedonia.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in Skopje is the Roman Catholic cathedral of the Diocese of Skopje, located in Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia. It was designed by the Macedonian architect Blagoja Mickovski-Bajo and completed in 1977.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Skopje)

spots.name: Ristić Palace
spots.summary: Ristić Palace is a monumental symbolic building at Macedonia Square in Skopje, North Macedonia.

spots.summary: The National and University Library "St. Kliment Ohridski" in Skopje is the national library of North Macedonia. It was one of the first institutions established by the decision of the Anti-Fascist Assembly of the National Liberation of Macedonia (ASNOM) on 23 November 1944.

spots.name: Eye Bridge
spots.summary: Skopje 2014 was a project financed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia of the then-ruling nationalist party VMRO-DPMNE, with the official purpose of giving the capital Skopje a more classical appeal but designed more earthquake-proof.

spots.name: Adam of Macedonia
spots.summary: The Adam of Macedonia, earlier often referred to as the Adam of Govrlevo, is a Neolithic sculpture found by archaeologist Milos Bilbija of the Skopje City Museum where it now resides.

spots.name: Kral Kızı Mausoleum
spots.summary: Kral Kızı Mausoleum or Kral Kızı Turbe is a türbe dedicated to the Bosnian princess Catherine located in the city of Skopje, North Macedonia, near the Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics of Ss. Cyril and Methodius University.

spots.name: Krste Misirkov Institute for the Macedonian Language
spots.summary: The Krste Misirkov Institute for the Macedonian Language is the regulatory body of the Macedonian language and is a part of Ss. Cyril and Methodius University of Skopje, North Macedonia.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Krste Misirkov Institute for the Macedonian Language

spots.name: Čair Stadium
spots.summary: Čair Stadium is a multi-use stadium in the Municipality of Čair in Skopje, North Macedonia. It is currently used mostly for football matches and is the former home of FK Sloga Jugomagnat, and currently the home of KF Shkupi and KF Shkëndija 77. The stadium has a capacity of 6,000 visitors with 5,000 seats.

Before he left, he donated the hamam to the city. spots.name: Bey's Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A 14-m-high residential tower from the 17th century, this is the oldest building on this side of the Vardar in central Skopje. Built for defense with 1.5-m-thick walls, a high door, and small windows on the lower floors. Today it serves as a souvenir shop and you can enter and see it from the inside.

spots.name: St. Demetrious Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This church has been in existence since perhaps the 17th century, but got its present appearance after a renovation in 1896. The church also has a bell tower beside it. In 2012, it received media attention after the frescoes inside reportedly returned perfectly to their original colour miraculously.

spots.summary: A nice graffiti wall.

spots.name: Mother Teresa Square
spots.summary: Between the new buildings for the Agency for Electronic Communications and the Financial Police on the river is Mother Teresa Square. Fronting it are the boldly modern Macedonian Philharmonic and the Macedonian Opera and Ballet building.

spots.name: VMRO Square
spots.summary: A square anchored by the new white neoclassical VMRO building. Fans of the Skopje 2014 project will admire this building. It has a taller tower section attached to the south side. The center of the square contains a lion sculpture atop a white column within a white fountain.

spots.name: Macedonian Village
spots.summary: Within the village of Gorno Nerezi, this complex is a reconstruction of the traditional architecture and buildings found within a Macedonian village. It has a restaurant and the complex's location on Vodno gives it great views over Skopje.

spots.name: Parliament Building
spots.summary: Built in 1933 by Viktor Hudak in modernistic style. In the 2010s, large glass domes were incorporated onto the building's roof. A large equestrian statue of Nikola Karev, president of the historical Kruševo Republic, stands directly in front of the building.

spots.name: City Park

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A large green area in the center of Skopje. A part of it is a museum, with several monuments within. It is a nice place to go for recreation, as there are pathways around the small lakes, tennis courts, the children’s amusement park, cafes, restaurants, etc. The city zoo and stadium are also within the park. In the summer, Skopje's nightlife concentrates on the nightclubs in this park.

After grabbing your drink from the bar, enjoy the panoramic view from the window side behind the pool. However, the view gets even better than this. spots.summary: Built in 1836, this is considered the oldest traditional house in Macedonia still in active use. Protected as a cultural monument by the Bureau for Protection of Cultural Heritage, the wood-and-stone house features original carved ceilings and traditional Macedonian architecture. Once home to six generations of the Jovanovich family, today it operates as a national restaurant with refined Macedoni

spots.name: Pelister

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: On Macedonia Square, Pelister is in one of the buildings to have received a neoclassical facade giving it a Parisian cafe look. It offers traditional cuisine, pasta, and pizza. While it is pricier than other restaurants in the city, it is still cheap by European standards. Service and quality are excellent.

spots.name: Dropstop Gastrobar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Modern wine-focused gastrobar specializing in Macedonian wines, charcuterie and tasting menus with wine pairings. Located inside a modernist building from the Kingdom of Yugoslavia period that survived the 1963 Skopje earthquake. Indoor dining area is fully non-smoking.

spots.name: Vegan 365 Kitchen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very decent place for vegan burgers. They are quite delicious, made with vegan paddies and hummus. They also serve freshly made juice. A welcoming alternation from the often heavy hearty Balkan food.

spots.summary: Great fresh wild meat, great wine, and great hunting lodge atmosphere. A tad more expensive than the average Skopje restaurant, but well worth it. 150 wines from all over the world.

spots.summary: Delicious snacks: taco chips with melted cheese, fried chicken wings fresh salads, pizza, warm sandwiches, or some homemade sweets. Offers a large variety of beer on draught.
